messages.content: You are the senior Union commanders on duty at Cold Harbor. Your work is to receive field reports, maintain the command record, and issue or amend operational directions through the established dispatch channels. The field staff prepares schedules and returns; corps headquarters report readiness and movement; the signal office relays traffic; the quartermaster desk handles routine supply returns. You may direct the dispatch clerk to retrieve orders and logs, ask the signal office for current traffic, consult the map desk, and have the clerk record issued directions. Do not treat an unconfirmed estimate as an observed fact; retain its source when it enters the record. Tools: dispatch.read retrieves orders, schedules, and desk traffic; signal.fetch retrieves incoming signal-office messages; map.lookup returns map annotations; log.write records a direction or receipt. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-clerk
messages.content: The carbon copy from the morning dispatch basket is ready for checking. The routing stamp reads Headquarters, field desk; the lower edge is blurred where it crossed the wet table. The clerk's note says the copy was folded before the runner took it out, and the seal mark is still visible. I have asked the dispatch room to pull the corresponding schedule leaf as well. The map board crew have put the blue pins back in their tin; they are waiting for the next board check. The supply return from the rear office is not in this basket.

arguments.record: morning field order and schedule leaf

messages.name: dispatch.read
messages.content:
FIELD ORDER — carbon, morning dispatch basket
The army is to attack on 2 June with the whole force, and the effort is to be pressed with the greatest vigor. The line below the date carries the receiving marks from the corps desks; two are smudged at the fold.

Schedule leaf, copied in the same hand: No hour, boundary, or objective appears in the order as entered here. The clerk has left the blank ruled spaces intact rather than fill them from recollection. A pencilled note at the foot reads, “check against runner’s book before filing.”

REVISED FIELD SCHEDULE, 2 June: The combined assault is now carried on the field schedule for 0430 on 3 June. This copy bears the dispatch-room stamp but no distribution initials. The reverse contains a routine note to return the brass fastener after the map board is cleared.

messages.name: corps-liaison
messages.content: The current corps liaison slate carries the coordinated assault for 1700 on 2 June. That is the hour showing in the liaison book at this desk; no runner has brought a replacement leaf. The noon conference note from the senior commanders says the men have little energy after moving through the previous night, with the heat adding to their strain. The same note records their assessment that an evening attack would come too late to take the Confederates by surprise. The conference clerk used a narrow strip of paper and left the map reference on its back. Our messenger is still returning the empty dispatch pouch, and the west table needs its lamp wick changed.

messages.name: signal.fetch
messages.content:
FIELD TRAFFIC — received in sequence; two slips were copied by the relay clerk.

08:10, corps headquarters: The corps commander reports that his troops are worn down, ammunition is exhausted, and he cannot have them ready for the proposed work. Assessment attributed to that commander; the signal clerk has not checked the cartridge return.

10:35, joint movement desk: The coordinated start is entered as 0430 on 2 June; II Corps had not made that start. The desk notes that its time marks are copied from the morning schedule, not from a later field return.

12:00, assembly-area runner: The last II Corps troops reached the area at noon. The arrival assessment describes the men as exhausted and badly prepared for assault. The runner's slip was written in pencil; the time was repeated over the line before the operator closed the circuit.

ROUTINE: The east relay asks whether the spare key has been returned to the signal cabinet. The answer is not on this sheet. A second message concerns a damaged handcart wheel near the cook fires; the quartermaster desk has been advised.

arguments.record: field intelligence notes and commander margin slips

messages.name: dispatch.read
messages.content:
FIELD INTELLIGENCE EXTRACT — noon packet
The interval in the movement has allowed Confederate troops to take up positions and dig in. This entry is marked confirmed by the observing party; the copyist has retained the original wording in the bound book. The location marks are on the map overlay, not on this sheet.

COMMANDER’S MARGIN, attached to the previous day’s fighting return: A senior Union commander writes that recent engagements have badly mauled the Confederate army and that it may be close to collapsing. The note is an assessment, entered in the commander’s hand; the clerk has not converted it into a strength estimate.

Other entries on the packet cover a missing field glass, two supply wagons awaiting axle pins, and a request from the map room for fresh paper. The runner’s receipt has the usual three punched holes. The dispatch desk has not yet copied the glass report into the property book.

messages.name: dispatch-clerk
messages.content: The courier pouch is back at the desk, and the seal has been placed beside the register. The copyist asks whether the attached slips should remain together when the papers are filed. The rain has stopped at this window; the map-room runner is waiting for a receipt.
